name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,177

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After combat an enlisted man gets spirit from bananas

blocks.note: combat between nations is war
the indefinite article as a single letter
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier back from the fighting reaches for a drink of banana liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the order: the soldier comes after the combat. WARAGI is a Ugandan spirit distilled from bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Waragi is the gin-like liquor made in Uganda by distilling fermented bananas.

clue.text: Tortilla or matzo possibly used in crazy meals

indicators.note: the letters are used inside the following words, sitting within them unchanged

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A query about whether flatbreads go into some wild dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: AZYME is unleavened bread; 'possibly' marks tortilla and matzo as examples rather than synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are flat breads baked without yeast, which is exactly what this rare word for unleavened bread names.

clue.text: The one here, having also called earlier, I answer in an agitated state

blocks.note: also known as, placed first because of 'earlier'
the one here is this one
taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone already phoned, and now the speaker replies in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: AKA (also known as) is how 'also called' becomes letters. AKATHISIA is a medical term for inner restlessness, often a drug side effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Akathisia is a clinical condition of restlessness, an inability to sit still, so it is an agitated state of body and mind.

clue.text: I deliver aluminium connected with parts for viewer

blocks.note: taken as written
to deliver someone from a thing is to rid them of it
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of delivering aluminium for components of a viewing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' sounds like a gadget, but it is the eye; its coloured parts are the irises.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridal is the adjective for the iris, the coloured part of the eye, and every viewer has two of them.

clue.text: Most passionate work ultimately happens before short nap

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the last letter of work
what happens is, in the sense of exists or takes place
siesta, an afternoon nap, cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: The most ardent effort comes just before a quick snooze.
explanation.walkthrough: SIESTA loses its last letter because the nap is 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissy means inclined to kissing or amorous, so its superlative fits the most passionate of lovers.

clue.text: Manufactured at York, cooler gift is put in trinket collection

indicators.note: something manufactured has been made up, so these letters are put together anew
the pieces are placed inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
the cooler and the nick are both slang for prison
a gift for something is a knack

explanation.surface: Something produced in York goes into a display of small ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged York letters split after their first letter to take the two pieces. The cooler and the nick are British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A knick-knackatory is a jocular word for a store or cabinet of small ornaments, a place holding many trinkets.

clue.text: Hawk moth bothered hind and pigs

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed and upset, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large moth pesters a female deer and some pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphingids are the family Sphingidae, the hawk moths, named for the sphinx-like resting pose of their caterpillars.

clue.text: Popular Italian monk appearing later in book?

blocks.note: what is popular is in
Fra is the Italian title for a friar or brother

explanation.surface: A well-liked Italian friar turns up in the closing chapters of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: INFRA is Latin for 'below', used in texts to refer the reader to a later passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers use the Latin word in footnotes, as in 'see infra', to send readers to a passage further on.

clue.text: Suddenly stressed notes showing how to get son from Zion?

blocks.note: the letter S that must come in
the swap instruction: one letter for another
Z, the letter that must make way
the further step joined on
I, the letter that must also go to leave the word for a male child

explanation.surface: Musical notes are accented sharply, apparently by a recipe for altering a biblical place name.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the instruction itself: to turn ZION into SON, put S for Z, and I is dropped, read as 'S for Z and I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sforzando marks a note to be played with a sudden strong accent; the Italian plural names several such notes.

clue.text: Sensual, extremely sexy area embraced by UK people

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word
one piece is held inside another as if hugged

blocks.note: the two outer letters of sexy
the people of the UK are the British
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A description of a hot corner of Britain where locals enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The area letter sits just after the first letter of the people. Sybaris was a Greek city famous for luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritish means given to luxury and sensual pleasure, after the pleasure-loving citizens of ancient Sybaris.

clue.text: Farmer’s first one that could fawn over tenanted land

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word before it
in a down-style turnover, over means read from the other end

blocks.note: the opening letter of farmer
a doe gives birth to a fawn, the verb to fawn meaning to bear young

explanation.surface: A farmer's prized animal is a creature that might grovel on its master's land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' looks like flattering behaviour, but here it is to give birth to a fawn. FEOD is a variant spelling of feud, in the sense of fief.
explanation.definitionFit: A feod, or feud, is land held from a lord in return for service, which is tenanted land in the feudal system.

clue.text: Soundly beat Lizzy and Scouse mate

blocks.note: Lizzy and Beth are both short forms of Elizabeth
wack is Liverpool slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Two people, a woman named Lizzy and a Liverpudlian chum, take a hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse means from Liverpool, whose dialect uses wack or whacker for pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bethwack is an old word meaning to thrash thoroughly, so it is to beat someone soundly.

clue.text: No provincial recalled entering Kiwi’s home by a lake in Africa

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
the turned word goes into the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: nay is the old or dialect form of no
a Kiwi is a New Zealander
taken as written

explanation.surface: A countryman's refusal is remembered as someone from New Zealand moves home beside an African lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed no word sits between N and Z. NYANZA is a Bantu word for a lake, found in names like Victoria Nyanza.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyanza is the word for a large lake in east-central Africa, as in the old names of Lake Victoria and Lake Albert.

clue.text: Goat’s head and gravy: things Shetlanders fiddled with

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of goat
jus is a thin gravy of meat juices

explanation.surface: An odd island menu of goat's head in gravy that Shetlanders tinkered with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddled' sounds like tampering, but it is literal: a GJU is an old Shetland fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gjus were the traditional two-stringed fiddles of Shetland, so they were instruments people there played with a bow.

clue.text: For an audience, a patient man records an average one

indicators.note: something done for an audience is heard rather than read on the page

blocks.note: Job, the Old Testament model of patience, plus logs for records

explanation.surface: A long-suffering man keeps diaries for listeners, as an ordinary bloke would.
explanation.walkthrough: Job is the biblical figure tested by God whose patience is proverbial. JOE BLOGGS is the British name for an average person, like the American John Doe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock British name for a typical member of the public, an unremarkable everyman.

clue.text: Smearing conveyed by note carried by Antipodean idiot

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it

blocks.note: nong is Australian slang for a fool
travelling in a car is being conveyed by it
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Slander spreads through a song via some Australian fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyed by' looks like a link word, but it supplies two letters. NOINTING is an old form of anointing.
explanation.definitionFit: To noint is an archaic shortening of anoint, to smear with oil or ointment.

clue.text: Irish tea mug with contents to guide piggish creature

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, with the outside ones discarded

blocks.note: tay is the Irish pronunciation and spelling of tea
a mug is a fool, an ass
the inner letters of guide

explanation.surface: A cup of Irish tea with something inside to steer by, offered to a pig-like animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' suggests a cup for the tea, but it means a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tayassuids are the peccaries, the family Tayassuidae of American mammals closely resembling pigs.

clue.text: Rest enlisting superior for a champion of old poet

indicators.note: enlisting brings a recruit into the ranks, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: to doze is to rest lightly
U means upper-class or superior in British usage
per means for each, as in so much per head

explanation.surface: A sleepy break takes in someone senior on behalf of a medieval hero.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class usage. The old poet is Spenser, who used DOUZEPER for one of Charlemagne's twelve peers.
explanation.definitionFit: The douzepers were the twelve paladins of Charlemagne, so the word in Spenser means a great knight or champion.

clue.text: Separating wild mice is unknown in Confucian way, relating to complex animals

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run free into a new order
the jumbled letters are split apart by what goes between them
the unknown sits inside the Chinese philosophy word

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
Tao, the Way, is a core idea of Chinese thought
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: Untamed rodents are kept apart in a puzzling oriental philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The reworked mice split after their second letter around the Way holding the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Metazoa are the many-celled animals with differentiated tissues, so metazoic describes complex animals rather than single-celled ones.

clue.text: Certainly dated by swains on a regular basis

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Courting youths certainly go out on dates with their sweethearts regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' looks like romance, but it marks the definition as archaic: YWIS is an old word for certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ywis is a Middle English adverb meaning surely or indeed, so it is an archaic way of saying certainly.

clue.text: Love feasts get on with an announcement system installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to get on in years is to age
the indefinite article
PA is a public address system

explanation.surface: Romantic banquets go ahead once a loudspeaker system is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' is to grow older here, not to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: The agapae were the communal meals of early Christians, called love feasts after the Greek agape, meaning love.

clue.text: Concerted effort to devour new crêpe

indicators.note: to devour is to swallow, taking something inside

blocks.note: a blitz is an intensive all-out effort
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A team rush to wolf down a freshly made pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A blintz is a thin pancake folded around a filling, which in Jewish cooking is a type of crêpe.

clue.text: God that presides in fourth book and 14th letter

blocks.note: Numbers, the fourth book of the Bible, is abbreviated Num
the 14th letter is N, spelt out as en

explanation.surface: A deity is said to be in charge in a particular book of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is spelt as its name, as printers call a half-em space an en.
explanation.definitionFit: A numen is the Roman idea of a presiding divinity or spirit that rules over a place or thing.

clue.text: A blow for Milton Keynes’ last couple after greatest Liberal’s left

indicators.note: having left, the party member is no longer present in the word
the last couple are the final two letters of the name

blocks.note: greatest in size is largest
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
the final pair of letters of Keynes

explanation.surface: A setback for the new town of Milton Keynes, and its top Liberal departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milton Keynes' reads as the English new town, but Milton is the poet and Keynes supplies letters. ARGESTES is the north-west wind in Paradise Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Argestes is the classical name for the north-west wind, which Milton names among the blasts in Paradise Lost; a wind is a blow.

clue.text: Penny-pinching father turns up besotted

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold of, so the father holds the coin
in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sire is a father
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A stingy dad arrives, head over heels in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny-pinching' reads as mean, but it splits into the coin and the grab. ÉPRIS is French for smitten.
explanation.definitionFit: Épris is a French borrowing meaning enamoured or captivated, used of someone smitten with another person.

clue.text: Ancient inscription’s crack returned in the morning

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: to have a crack at something is to have a go
am is ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A fissure in an old carved text reappeared one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests a split in stone, but it means an attempt. OGAM, or ogham, is the early Irish alphabet carved on stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogam is the old Celtic script of notches cut along stone edges, found on ancient memorial inscriptions.

clue.text: Concert probe impertinently keeping back half of author’s fact-book

indicators.note: half of a word means just its front portion is taken
back means the letters are put the wrong way round
keeping means holding something within

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
to pry is to poke nosily into others' business
the first three of the word's six letters

explanation.surface: A nosy concert-goer peers into a writer's reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer series of London concerts. PROMPTUARY is an old word for a handbook of facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A promptuary is a storehouse of information, a handbook from which facts may be quickly drawn, so a fact-book.

clue.text: Lack of coordination could make one angry, yes?

indicators.note: the words could be made into one new word by remaking their letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clumsiness is something that can get a person cross, can't it?
explanation.definitionFit: Asynergy is the medical term for faulty coordination between muscles or organs that normally act together.

clue.text: Eatable grass in some places eastward, with no filling item on menu

indicators.note: without its filling only the outer shell of the word remains

blocks.note: the first and last letters of eastward
a dish is a single item on a menu

explanation.surface: A regional menu offers grass as a meal, served eastward without stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some places' is part of the definition: EDDISH is a dialect word for the aftermath, grass that regrows after mowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddish is a regional English term for the second growth of grass after a hay crop, good for grazing.
